$comment: Rails for the Ralph loop's executor when its runner is `claude` — the
`claude -p` process `ralph/delegate.sh` starts. Loaded only through
`--settings` from that script, so it never touches an interactive session
or the user's own settings. `ralph/opencode-executor.jsonc` is the same rail for
the opencode runner: every bash deny there has its counterpart here, and
this file then denies what only Claude Code offers — web tools, the Agent
tool, inter-agent messaging, background monitors and scheduling,
worktrees, artifacts, and the skills that deploy, touch a database, drive
a browser or desktop, or hand work to another agent. MCP is not on
this list because no pattern covers a server: `delegate.sh` passes
`--strict-mcp-config`, and the probe reads `init.mcp_servers` off the
stream to prove it came up empty.
Every Bash deny is written twice, `Bash(x *)` and `Bash(x:*)`: the two
are the space-separated and colon-separated spellings of one prefix rule,
and which one a given CLI version honours has moved. The probe proves
the pair bites; it does not say which half did.
The executor runs with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, which approves
anything not denied here — so this list IS the rail, exactly as the
opencode file's `"*": "allow"` catch-all makes its deny list the rail.
That a settings-file deny still bites under bypass was PROBED, not read:
`ralph/claude-executor-rails-probe.sh` asks a live Sonnet to run `gh` and
expects the refusal. Run it after touching this file or upgrading the CLI.
What it cannot do: confine Bash to the checkout. opencode's
`external_directory` denies a shell command that names an outside path;
Claude Code has no such setting, so the `Bash(* ~/.x/*)` lines below are
pattern tripwires on the stores somebody thought of — probed to bite on
`ls`, `cat` and `head` in the `~/` and `$HOME` spellings — not a boundary.
The boundary is `env -i`: the executor receives no secret to leak, and
every store it could reach is one the orchestrator, on the same model
family, already holds.
